articles.title: LOFAR Takes the Deepest Image of the Low-Frequency Radio Sky to Date
articles.description: Using the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR), an international team led by Leiden University has produced the sharpest and most sensitive radio image of the sky ever made at low radio frequencies.
articles.summary: LOFAR captures the deepest and sharpest low-frequency radio sky image to date, opening unprecedented views of the universe's radio-emitting phenomena.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks
articles.description: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed complex organic carbon just beneath the surface of ancient Martian rocks, raising intriguing questions about the Red Planet's potential to have supported life. The remarkable preservation of these compounds, along with similar discoveries thousands of miles away, suggests the building blocks of life may once have been widespread across Mars.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover confirms complex organic carbon beneath ancient Martian rocks, revealing a key ingredient for life on the Red Planet.

articles.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies. Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.
articles.summary: A groundbreaking supercomputer simulation reveals how the universe emerged from its cosmic dark age and transformed into the cosmos we observe today.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
articles.description: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 astronauts launched to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: Apollo 12 launched on November 14, 1969, achieving a historic pinpoint lunar landing that demonstrated NASA's precision in human spaceflight.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
articles.description: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars.  Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars on November 13, 1971, revolutionizing our understanding of the Red Planet with unprecedented close-up imagery.

articles.title: Outbursts from a Massive Star
articles.description: Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star located in the galaxy shown in this image released on Nov. 9, 2026. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the […]
articles.summary: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory has identified the mechanism triggering repeated outbursts from a massive star, advancing our understanding of stellar dynamics and high-energy phenomena.

articles.title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
articles.description: Astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. orbited Earth from November 11 to 15, 1966, on Gemini XII, the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. In addition to successfully completing rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures vital to sending American astronauts to the Moon, the crew was also spurring the development of […]
articles.summary: Historic Gemini XII mission photographs by astronauts Lovell and Aldrin inspired the development of early Earth observation programs, demonstrating the scientific value of human spaceflight.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope reveals a diverse gallery of gravitational lenses that will serve as valuable targets for the upcoming Roman Space Telescope.

articles.title: When Einstein's Gravitational Waves Meet Newton's Tides
articles.description: A researcher at Freie Universität Berlin has developed a theoretical framework for searching high-precision measurements for possible relativistic traces in lunar tides.
articles.summary: A researcher has developed a theoretical framework bridging Einstein's gravitational waves with Newtonian tidal mechanics, enabling new high-precision measurement techniques.

articles.title: Astrophysicists Cross Another Dark Matter Candidate Off Their List: Stupendously Large Black Holes
articles.description: Astrophysicists are leaving no stone unturned in their search for what dark matter is. Different particles have been proposed, like WIMPs and axions. Hypothetical rimordial black holes have also been proposed. But there's another less well-known candidate, SLABs or Stupendously Large Black holes, a sub-type of primordial black holes. Alas, SLABs can't account for dark matter either, according to new research.
articles.summary: Astrophysicists eliminate stupendously large black holes as a dark matter candidate, narrowing the search for this cosmic mystery through rigorous theoretical constraints.

articles.title: Dense Galaxy Clusters Foster Mechanisms That Throttle Star Formation
articles.description: The Cosmic Noon was when the Universe's Stelliferous Era Began, and star formation was prodigious during that epoch. But since then, star formation has slowed to a relative crawl, despite the fact that we can watch them forming in regions throughout the Milky Way. What happened to the hydrogen gas that forms stars? New research found clues in a particulary dense galaxy cluster.
articles.summary: Research reveals how dense galaxy clusters regulate star formation through physical mechanisms, providing insights into cosmic evolution during the universe's most active epochs.

articles.title: Shape-Shifting Robotic "Slugs" Could One Day Crawl Across Alien Worlds
articles.description: Robots have been a mainstay of our early space exploration efforts. But they normally have wheels. Or in some cases, rotors. While those solutions are great on flat ground, they struggle with jagged boulders or tight crevices. So engineers have been working on alternative robotic form factors, and a recent paper in Nature Machine Intelligence from researchers at Colorado State University’s Adaptive Robotics Lab, describes a unique morphology using a design principle typically seen in architecture rather than robotics - tensegrity.
articles.summary: Innovative shape-shifting robotic slugs could revolutionize future space exploration by offering new mobility solutions for traversing diverse alien worlds.

articles.title: Euclid's First Data Release: A Stepping Stone to its 3D Map of the Sky
articles.description: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has released its first huge batch of data. It's all part of the telescope's mission to study dark energy and dark matter. The telescope is busy creating the largest ever 3D map of the Universe with its huge 600 megapixel camera, and new images give us some highlights.
articles.summary: ESA's Euclid Space Telescope releases its first major data batch as part of its mission to create a 3D map of the sky, advancing our understanding of the universe's structure.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster explosion prevents an unprecedented double catch
articles.description: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico and exploded Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: SpaceX achieves a major milestone by launching Starship into orbit, despite an unprecedented double-catch attempt being thwarted by booster loss.

articles.title: A likely supermassive neutron star might shed light on the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes
articles.description: A team of astronomers recently identified a red giant star with an unseen binary companion after examining data from the Large Sky Area MultiObject Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). Although the companion object can't be observed visually, astronomers can see the gravitational effects it has on the red giant star.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers identify a likely supermassive neutron star that could illuminate the mysterious mass gap between neutron stars and black holes.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship 'catch'
articles.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking "catch" of the spaceship following a day in orbit.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship test prepares to attempt a groundbreaking first-ever spaceship 'catch' of the world's most powerful rocket.

articles.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered a potentially enormous new dwarf planet beyond Pluto, hidden for years in one of the most crowded regions of the night sky. The discovery of 2026 ED138 could expand the solar system's official dwarf planet family and hints that more mysterious worlds may be lurking far beyond Neptune.
articles.summary: Astronomers discover a potentially enormous new dwarf planet hidden beyond Pluto, potentially becoming our sixth dwarf planet.

articles.title: Dark energy may have flipped from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago
articles.description: A mysterious force driving the expansion of the Universe may have undergone a dramatic reversal billions of years ago. Scientists exploring an overlooked branch of an alternative gravity theory discovered that dark energy could have switched from negative to positive roughly 9.5 billion years ago, potentially changing how we understand cosmic history.
articles.summary: Dark energy may have dramatically reversed from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago, offering new insights into the universe's expansion.

articles.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
articles.description: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.
articles.summary: Scientists reveal that Earth's water may have originated in the planet's fiery early atmosphere rather than from cosmic delivery by comets or asteroids.

articles.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields
articles.description: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has revealed a surprising secret hidden within the chaos of space: turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation when examined at extremely small scales. The discovery exposes an unexpected pattern in solar wind turbulence that could help scientists better understand solar activity and predict geomagnetic storms.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe uncovers a hidden pattern within the Sun's turbulent magnetic fields, advancing our understanding of solar dynamics.

articles.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
articles.description: After more than a year of simulated life on Mars, four NASA volunteers have finally emerged from isolation, bringing a remarkable space exploration experiment to an end. Their experiences growing food, conserving resources, and overcoming Mars-like challenges could help NASA prepare for humanity's future on the Moon and Mars.
articles.summary: NASA's CHAPEA Mars simulation crew completes over a year of isolated habitat training, successfully emerging with valuable data for future human Mars missions.

articles.title: Watch SpaceX will attempt its 1st-ever 'chopsticks' Starship landing catch of a rocket from orbit today (livestream)
articles.description: SpaceX plans to catch the upper stage of its Starship megarocket at the launch pad today (Nov. 14), and you can watch the unprecedented action live.
articles.summary: SpaceX attempts its first-ever 'chopsticks' booster catch maneuver during Starship's upper stage recovery in an innovative test of reusable rocket technology.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
articles.description: SpaceX's Starship megarocket reached orbit today (Nov. 13) during its 15th test flight, but the company scrapped a plan to catch the vehicle's massive booster back at the launch site.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 successfully reached orbit on November 13 during an ambitious 22-hour test flight, advancing the development of humanity's most powerful megarocket.

articles.title: Scientists discover mysterious radio signals coming every eight minutes from deep space
articles.description: Astronomers in have linked the regular radio pulses to an unusual pairing of celestial bodies 5,000 light-years from Earth.
articles.summary: Astronomers have linked mysterious radio signals pulsing every eight minutes from 5,000 light-years away to an unusual pairing of celestial bodies, expanding our understanding of cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA opens applications for astronauts selected to live and work on the Moon, offering an unprecedented opportunity for space exploration careers.

articles.title: SpaceX intentará por primera vez atrapar a su Starship con sus 'palillos chinos'
articles.description: La compañía de Elon Musk quiere recuperar por primera vez las dos etapas de su megacohete con sus 'palillos chinos' mientras la NASA sigue esperándolo para volver a la Luna
articles.summary: SpaceX attempts its first catch of both Starship stages using mechanical 'chopsticks' arms, a major milestone in full rocket reusability.

articles.title: Historische Premiere: Roboter setzt eigenständig eine Struktur im Weltraum zusammen
articles.description: Ohne Menschen vor Ort hat ein Roboter im All autonom ein Bauteil errichtet. Es könnte der Anfang roboterbasierten Baus im Orbit sein.
articles.summary: A robot autonomously assembles a structure in space for the first time, marking a historic milestone in robotic space construction.

articles.title: SpaceX is trying to solve a decades-old challenge: Making rockets fully reusable
articles.description:
SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 launches at Starbase in Texas on September 28, 2026 (RONALDO SCHEMIDT)
Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreakin…
articles.summary: SpaceX works toward full rocket reusability with Starship, tackling one of spaceflight's greatest engineering challenges.

articles.title: SpaceX is set to make an audacious grab for ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here are the risks
articles.description: A crucial test this week could bring SpaceX one step closer to revolutionizing spaceflight — or cast new uncertainty on the company’s boldest ambitions. SpaceX will for the first time attempt to bring every part of its massive Starship, the most powerful rock…
articles.summary: SpaceX pursues an audacious test to achieve the 'holy grail' of rocketry, potentially revolutionizing spaceflight economics and capability.

articles.title: Asteroid Bennu's Sample Delivers Another Surprise
articles.description: Researchers compared the samples from asteroid Bennu with the Murchison meteorite and measured the amino acid β-alanine in both. Using new techniques, they were able to measure not only their isotopic compositions, but isotopic differences between individual …
articles.summary: Asteroid Bennu samples reveal amino acid β-alanine, providing insights into the building blocks of life and the composition of early solar system materials.
